claim_type_rationale: Deterministic universe rule with two upstream source-defined anchors: (a) the 12-constellation universe is anchored by Wikipedia's `Zodiac` master article (which identifies the twelve constellations after which the twelve zodiac signs are named, in canonical ecliptic order); (b) per-constellation row-membership + ranking + value cells are anchored by the 12 dedicated `List of stars in <Constellation>` ranked-list articles (each table is sorted by apparent magnitude with Name / Apparent Magnitude / Spectral Class columns). The 'three brightest by apparent magnitude per constellation' rule is a total ordering on a closed set — no curator judgment after these two anchors. The deterministic-universe-rule preference (see instance_selection_priorities.md::Fast viability gate) is satisfied: SQL-WHERE-clause is `constellation IN (12-zodiac-set) AND magnitude_rank_within_constellation <= 3`. Distinct from `candidate_rebuild` (no curator-bounded universe selection) and distinct from `partially_supplemented` (no rebuilding of any source subset).

collection_summary.approach: Pre-curation design pass (cycle-0 source exploration + audit-cycle-1 design review APPROVE-WITH-AMENDMENTS) produced a source-faithful instance with all 4 design blockers from audit-cycle-1 resolved before staging. Cycle-0 verified Zodiac master + per-constellation prose pages exist, but the preliminary slate had factual errors under a per-constellation-prose-page source rule (Aries 3rd = Mesarthim was wrong; should be 41 Ari per the ranked List_of_stars_in_Aries; Pisces 3rd = Alrescha was wrong; should be ω Psc per the ranked List_of_stars_in_Pisces). Audit-cycle-1 amendment #1 redirected the row-defining source family to the 12 dedicated `List of stars in <Constellation>` ranked-list pages (which expose Name + Apparent Magnitude + Spectral Class in sorted order). Universe was rebuilt entirely from those 12 list pages via per-constellation WebFetch verification before staging.
collection_summary.partition_structure: 12 constellations after which the twelve zodiac signs are named × 3 lowest-apparent-magnitude stars per constellation = 36 rows. Composite PK (Constellation, Star). Each constellation's partition has exactly 3 rows.

roles.role_note: universe: identifies the twelve constellations after which the twelve zodiac signs are named (Aries through Pisces) in canonical ecliptic order. The Zodiac article also explicitly notes that the ecliptic intersects Ophiuchus in addition to the 12 zodiac-namesake constellations — Ophiuchus is OUT of scope under the staged 'zodiac-namesake' framing (decision_log).
universe + ranking + value for Aries: ranked table by apparent magnitude; top 3 = Hamal, β Ari, 41 Ari with magnitudes + spectral classes verbatim.
universe + ranking + value for Taurus: top 3 = Aldebaran, β Tau, Alcyone A.
universe + ranking + value for Gemini: top 3 = Pollux, Castor A, γ Gem.
universe + ranking + value for Cancer: top 3 = β Cnc, δ Cnc, ι Cnc A (note: Cancer is the dimmest zodiac constellation; brightest star is only magnitude 3.53).
universe + ranking + value for Leo: top 3 = Regulus, Denebola, γ1 Leo (Algieba). Note: γ Leo is a binary system; the list page rows are split by component (γ1 Leo is the brighter component).
universe + ranking + value for Virgo: top 3 = Spica, γ Vir A, ε Vir.
universe + ranking + value for Libra: top 3 = β Lib, α2 Lib, σ Lib (note: Libra's brightest is β not α; α Lib is a double-star system with α1 + α2 components).
universe + ranking + value for Scorpius: top 3 = Antares A, λ Sco, θ Sco.
universe + ranking + value for Sagittarius: top 3 = ε Sgr, σ Sgr, ζ Sgr. Note: ε Sgr (Kaus Australis) is brighter than α Sgr in Sagittarius — α Sgr is not in the top 3.
universe + ranking + value for Capricornus: top 3 = δ Cap, β1 Cap, α2 Cap. Note: Capricornus's brightest is δ (Deneb Algedi), not α (Algedi); α Cap is a double-star system.
universe + ranking + value for Aquarius: top 3 = β Aqr, α Aqr, δ Aqr. Note: Aquarius's brightest is β (Sadalsuud), narrowly brighter than α (Sadalmelik) at 2.90 vs 2.95.

universe + ranking + value for Pisces: top 3 = η Psc, γ Psc, ω Psc. Note: Pisces α (Alrescha) is NOT in the top 3; it appears later in the ranked list. Audit-cycle-1 caught this factual error in the cycle-0 preliminary slate.

source_coverage_notes.validation_only_sources: The 12 per-constellation prose pages (Aries (constellation), Taurus (constellation), ..., Pisces (constellation)) and per-star Wikipedia articles (Hamal, Aldebaran, Pollux, etc.) are validation-only context and are NOT registered in source_urls per the artifact contract (validation sources do not count toward source_count and live in provenance prose). The per-constellation prose pages are non-uniform — they don't expose a clean ranked top-3 table — which is why audit-cycle-1 redirected the row-defining source family to the dedicated `List of stars in <Constellation>` ranked-list pages.
source_coverage_notes.source_grounding_summary: 1 registered Zodiac master (roles = [universe]; defines the 12-zodiac-namesake set + ecliptic order) + 12 registered `List of stars in <Constellation>` ranked-list pages (roles = [universe, ranking, value]; each supplies the 3-brightest enumeration with Name / Magnitude / Spectral Class verbatim) = 13 URLs total. Validation-only sources (12 per-constellation prose pages, 36 per-star pages) live in source_coverage_notes prose, NOT in source_urls.

decision_log.decision: claim_type = source_defined (per audit-cycle-1 design review; deterministic-universe-rule preference satisfied)
decision_log.rationale: The universe rule is deterministic and source-defined: 12-zodiac-namesake universe per Zodiac master + 3-lowest-apparent-magnitude ranking per list-article. No curator judgment after the two source-defined anchors. Distinct from `candidate_rebuild` (no curator-bounded universe selection) and distinct from `partially_supplemented` (no rebuilding of source subset). SQL-WHERE-clause expressible: `constellation IN (12-zodiac-set) AND magnitude_rank_within_constellation <= 3`.

decision_log.decision: Row-defining source family = 12 `List of stars in <Constellation>` ranked-list pages (NOT per-constellation prose pages)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 amendment #1: the per-constellation prose pages (Aries (constellation), etc.) are not uniform ranked tables — they discuss the constellation's history, mythology, brightest stars, deep-sky objects, etc., but don't expose a clean top-3-by-magnitude enumeration. The dedicated `List of stars in <Constellation>` pages are explicitly sorted by decreasing brightness and supply the Name + Apparent Magnitude + Spectral Class columns verbatim. The preliminary cycle-0 slate (which used per-constellation prose pages as the row-defining source) had factual errors: Aries 3rd row was Mesarthim (γ Ari, magnitude 3.86) but the ranked list-article correctly identifies 41 Ari (magnitude 3.61) as 3rd; Pisces 3rd row was Alrescha (α Psc, 3.82) but the ranked list-article identifies ω Psc (4.03) as 3rd. Switching to the list-article source family eliminates these errors and makes source_defined defensible.

decision_log.decision: Universe = 12 constellations after which the twelve zodiac signs are named (NOT '12 zodiac constellations' loose framing)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 amendment #3: the Zodiac article explicitly distinguishes 'the twelve constellations after which the twelve zodiac signs are named' from 'the 13 constellations of Ptolemy's Almagest...that the ecliptic intersects' (which includes Ophiuchus). The staged title uses the more precise namesake framing. Ophiuchus is OUT of scope — it intersects the ecliptic but is NOT a zodiac-sign-namesake.

decision_log.decision: Constellation cell values = astronomical Latin forms (Scorpius, Capricornus); zodiac-sign forms (Scorpio, Capricorn) NOT used
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 amendment #3: the Zodiac master article uses sign forms (Scorpio, Capricorn) in its zodiac-sign column, but the per-constellation list-article titles use astronomical Latin forms (List of stars in Scorpius, List of stars in Capricornus). The staged Constellation cell follows the astronomical Latin convention because (a) the list-article titles use it, (b) the per-constellation prose pages also use it, (c) astronomical reference databases (IAU, Hipparcos, etc.) use it. The Zodiac→Latin normalization is: Scorpio→Scorpius, Capricorn→Capricornus.

decision_log.decision: Star cell values = list-article Name column VERBATIM (NOT curator-judgment proper-name-preference)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4: the cycle-0 design proposed 'proper name where available, Bayer designation fallback' which invites curator choice. The staged form uses the list-article Name cell verbatim, yielding a deterministic mix: Hamal + β Ari + 41 Ari in Aries (rather than the curator-preferred Hamal + Sheratan + Gamma Arietis). This is less aesthetic but source-faithful and audit-friendly. The list-article Name column makes the choice for us: some rows are proper names (Hamal, Aldebaran, Pollux, Regulus, Spica, Antares A, Denebola, Castor A), others are Bayer designations (β Ari, 41 Ari, γ Gem, β Cnc, etc.). The mix is deterministic per the source.

decision_log.decision: Spectral Class cell values = full source-faithful classification (NOT letter-only)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 design review: the list pages already expose Spectral Class with full classification detail (e.g., 'M1.5Iab-b' for Antares A, 'A5mF2 (IV)' for δ Cap, 'M3/M4III' for σ Lib, 'B2IV+DA7.9' for λ Sco). Letter-only (M, A, etc.) would discard source-defined detail and require curator-judgment truncation. Staged form preserves the full classification verbatim from each list page.

decision_log.decision: Variable-star magnitude = single scalar catalogue value from list page (NOT a range cell)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 design review: several brightest zodiac stars are variable (Antares α Sco varies ~0.6–1.6; Algol-type binaries; etc.). The list pages already use a single scalar magnitude (either mean or catalogue value) per row. The staged form follows that — single scalar per row, with variability documented in provenance/spectral-class notes (e.g., Denebola spectral class 'A3Vvar' explicitly notes variability). No range-valued cell.

decision_log.decision: Sort = zodiac-position ASC primary (Aries=1, Pisces=12), Apparent Magnitude ASC secondary
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 design review: lexicographic Constellation sort would give 'Aquarius, Aries, Cancer, Capricornus, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Pisces, Sagittarius, Scorpius, Taurus, Virgo' — incorrect. The canonical ecliptic order (Aries → Pisces) is the Zodiac article's own enumeration order. The db_analog uses `z.zodiac_position` numeric column (1-12) for the primary sort. Within each constellation, Apparent Magnitude ASC (brightest first) per the list-article's own ordering. Same pattern as periodic-table-groups numeric-parse-from-Group-N sort.

Per audit-cycle-1 design review: the Zodiac article notes 'the ecliptic intersects with 13 constellations of Ptolemy's Almagest, as well as of the more precisely delineated IAU designated constellations. In addition to the twelve constellations after which the twelve zodiac signs are named, the ecliptic intersects Ophiuchus.' Ophiuchus is NOT a zodiac-sign-namesake; the staged universe is the 12-zodiac-namesake set. Documented here for transparency — analogous to f-block lanthanides/actinides exclusion in periodic-table-groups.

Per the answer-entity-wins policy (instance_selection_priorities.md::Classification policy): for the composite PK (Constellation, Star), Constellation is the scaffold partition (1-12 zodiac position) and Star is the answer entity. Stars are naturally-occurring celestial objects classified by attributes (magnitude, spectral class, distance), same bucket as moons (`taxonomic-entities/moons` in `planets_named_moons`), species, nutrients. Extends taxonomic-entities/* bucket from 3 to 4 instances (joining moons, species, nutrients). The under-represented bucket gets a NEW fine-class.

normalization_decisions.rule: Astronomical Latin form per per-constellation `List of stars in <Constellation>` article title (and per-constellation prose page title). 12 values in zodiac ecliptic order: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpius, Sagittarius, Capricornus, Aquarius, Pisces. (NOT zodiac-sign forms 'Scorpio'/'Capricorn' which appear in the Zodiac article's sign-name column.) Sort by numeric zodiac-position 1-12 (per Zodiac master ecliptic order), NOT lexicographic.

List-article Name column VERBATIM. Deterministic mix of proper names (Hamal, Aldebaran, Pollux, Castor A, Regulus, Denebola, Spica, Antares A, Alcyone A) and Bayer designations (β Ari, 41 Ari, γ Gem, β Cnc, δ Cnc, ι Cnc A, γ1 Leo, γ Vir A, ε Vir, β Lib, α2 Lib, σ Lib, λ Sco, θ Sco, ε Sgr, σ Sgr, ζ Sgr, δ Cap, β1 Cap, α2 Cap, β Aqr, α Aqr, δ Aqr, η Psc, γ Psc, ω Psc). Greek letters preserved in Unicode (α, β, γ, δ, ε, ζ, η, θ, ι, κ, λ, σ, ω). Flamsteed numbers preserved (41 Ari). 'A' / '1' / '2' component suffixes preserved for binary/multiple systems (Antares A, Castor A, Alcyone A, γ Vir A, ι Cnc A, γ1 Leo, α2 Lib, β1 Cap, α2 Cap).

Float, single scalar per row, taken verbatim from list-article Apparent Magnitude column. Range in the staged set: 0.87 (Aldebaran, brightest) to 4.03 (ι Cnc A and ω Psc, tied dimmest within their constellations' top-3). Variable-star catalogue mean/peak used (not a range); variability documented in Spectral Class column where present (e.g., 'A3Vvar' for Denebola, 'G8IIIvar' for ε Vir). Sort within constellation: ASC (brightest first, lowest value first). Leading '+' sign dropped from positive values (e.g., '+1.85' → '1.85').

Full classification verbatim from list-article Spectral Class column. Examples: 'K2III', 'A5V...', 'B8Vn', 'K5III', 'B7III', 'K0III', 'A2Vm', 'A0IV', 'K4III', 'G8IIIa', 'B7V', 'A3Vvar', 'B1V', 'F0V+...', 'G8IIIvar', 'B8V', 'A3IV', 'M3/M4III', 'M1.5Iab-b', 'B2IV+DA7.9', 'F1II', 'B9IVp', 'B2.5V', 'A5mF2 (IV)', 'A5:n', 'G6/G8III', 'G0Ib', 'G2Ib', 'G7III', 'G8III', 'F4IV'. Composite classifications (e.g., '+DA7.9', '+...', '...' trailing, '/', ':') preserved per source. Letter-only simplification REJECTED at audit-cycle-1 because it would require curator-judgment truncation of source-defined detail.

open_questions.question: Should the staged set use modern catalogue magnitudes (e.g., Hipparcos) instead of Wikipedia list-page magnitudes if they differ?
open_questions.answer: No — the staged source rule is list-article Apparent Magnitude column verbatim. The Wikipedia list pages are themselves drawn from authoritative catalogues (Hipparcos, Tycho-2, SIMBAD) but may have slight variations. Per the source-rule, the list page is canonical. If audit prefers Hipparcos-direct values, the source rule would need to switch (changing claim_type framing).

open_questions.question: Should the staged set acknowledge stars with magnitude precision issues (e.g., binary systems where the listed magnitude is the combined system vs single component)?
open_questions.answer: Per per-list-page values: the list pages already document this — some rows are component-specific (Antares A, Castor A, γ1 Leo, β1 Cap, α2 Cap) and the magnitude is the component's individual magnitude per source. The staged set preserves the source's choice. Audit may want to flag specific rows where the source's component-vs-system framing is ambiguous.

cycle_1_audit_design_review.verdict: APPROVE WITH AMENDMENTS (4 design blockers + several keep/refinement notes)
amendments: 1. Row-defining source family = 12 dedicated `List of stars in <Constellation>` ranked-list pages (NOT per-constellation prose pages). The list pages are explicitly sorted by decreasing brightness and expose Name + Apparent Magnitude + Spectral Class columns verbatim.

2. Universe was rebuilt entirely from the 12 list pages — preliminary cycle-0 slate had factual errors: Aries 3rd was Mesarthim (γ, 3.86), correct is 41 Ari (3.61); Pisces 3rd was Alrescha (α, 3.82), correct is ω Psc (4.03). All 36 rows re-verified per list-article enumeration.

3. Universe scope reframed from '12 zodiac constellations' (slightly loose — also matches Ophiuchus on the ecliptic) to 'the 12 constellations after which the twelve zodiac signs are named' (matches master Zodiac article's exact framing). Ophiuchus exclusion documented in decision_log.

4. Star cell rule = list-article Name column VERBATIM (NOT curator-judgment 'proper name where available'). Yields deterministic mix (Hamal + β Ari + 41 Ari in Aries) — source-faithful, audit-friendly.

Keep: Spectral Class full classification (not letter-only); single scalar magnitude per row for variable stars (not range); zodiac-order primary sort + apparent-magnitude ASC secondary; entity class taxonomic-entities/stars under answer-entity-wins policy.
